title: Design a Distributed Rate Limiter
description: Design a multi-tenant rate-limiting service for an API gateway with explicit burst, refill, atomicity and outage semantics.
functionalRequirements: Enforce per-tenant and per-user API policies
Allow a configured burst while limiting sustained request rate
Return an allow/deny decision and a useful retry delay
Update policies without resetting all client budgets accidentally
nonFunctionalRequirements: Rate-limit decision p95 below 5 ms within the serving region
99.99% decision-path availability target, with endpoint-specific outage policy
Concurrent checks for the same key must update the budget atomically
constraints: 100000 average checks/s across tenants; plan for a 3x peak of 300000 checks/s
Example policy: 100 requests per minute with a burst capacity of 20 tokens
Size for 20 million active tenant-user-route buckets at 80 logical bytes each before object and key overhead
outOfScope: DDoS mitigation at network line rate
Billing-grade globally exact quotas without discussing the added coordination cost
A requirement to use Redis, Lua or a particular cloud vendor

scale.assumption: Synthetic interview workload, not a claim about any named company's actual traffic.

stateEstimates.name: Active logical bucket state before key and allocator overhead

notes: The example refill rate is 100/60 tokens per second, approximately 1.67; initial capacity is 20, not 100.
The daily check count is a sustained capacity scenario, not a count of unique users.
A fixed-window implementation is valid only if its larger boundary bursts are explicitly accepted; it does not silently satisfy token-bucket semantics.
